modality_prompt:
Use raw RGB together with the annotated view and detection list to judge the scene. Detections may be wrong or incomplete; missing detections do not mean absence. Verify person detections in RGB before treating them as civilians; robots or equipment may be mislabeled. The detector also checks fire extinguisher and robot dog (including nozzle/quadruped aliases); strongly overlapping person/equipment masks may be filtered before annotation and target creation. This visual conflict filter is heuristic, not confirmed civilian identity; unmatched or ambiguous detections still require RGB verification. During-action captures provide raw RGB only. Ending surroundings provide raw RGB followed by an annotated image only when annotation_available is true; otherwise only raw RGB is sent. The detection list remains available for both.
The label list distinguishes category=object/person/fire and includes label, confidence, pixel bbox_xyxy and grounding_available. Pixel boxes use the original RGB dimensions. Person labels do not establish NPC identity, health or a confirmed pose. A fire's attached_to is a same-frame visual association with an object/person target_ref, not an Oracle burning-state confirmation. When grounded, fire uses the attached target's coordinate (grounding_source=attached_target), not flame depth. An unknown attachment remains null. Objects and people use grounding_source=mask_depth when grounded. distance_xy_m is an estimated horizontal straight-line distance in meters from this frame's observing robot at capture time to the grounded target representative point, rounded to 0.1 m; null means unknown, never zero or nearby. It is not camera-forward depth, a path length, distance to the nearest object edge, or proof of interaction range or reachability. Fire distances inherit the attached target's grounding. An undetected target selected through pixel fallback has no list distance. Use distance with the existing proximity guidance: approach before proximity-dependent actions when far or proximity is unclear; the approximately 2 m guideline is not a guaranteed UE success radius. A historical frame's distance is not current proximity evidence after movement. Prefer an exact current target_ref with grounding_available=true when it reliably identifies the intended target. If SAM misses the target, has no grounding, or gives an unreliable association, choose a pixel from an actionable original RGB instead. Never execute an ungrounded or remembered entity reference. Each capture has frame_ref, width and height; when an annotation is supplied, its raw and annotated images show the same capture, in raw then annotated order. Only image_role=raw with actionable=true supplies pixel targets. Copy frame_ref exactly and use integer pixel_xy=[u,v] in original RGB dimensions: origin at top-left, u rightward, v downward, 0<=u<width and 0<=v<height. For navigation choose standable ground near the target; for suppression choose a visible burning solid surface near the fire base, avoiding flame and smoke pixels. Valid depth is geometry only, not evidence of burning or reachability. If no reliable target or point is visible, approach or observe again. Only the current ending surroundings batch is actionable; periodic captures and memory cannot supply action targets. Do not invent references or coordinates. Matching class labels across frames do not establish identity. The executor resolves coordinates. Treat precise health as unknown unless explicitly reported.
Frames follow during_action, then surroundings; use their timestamps to distinguish route history from the ending observation. Visual suppression has no automatic fire-state verification: after a command executes, its effect report is unknown. An execution failure or rejected target means suppression was not confirmed to run; an unknown visual effect must not be interpreted as successful spraying or extinguishing. Interpret the images as visual evidence without treating them as a programmatic fire_extinguished confirmation.
Follower feedback and following_npcs use system-supplied civilian names; newly_following_npcs identifies additions to the prior report.
